The ending feels entirely natural and earned because it directly resolves the narrator's central internal conflict, which the entire story has been building toward. Since college, the narrator has idolized and resented Q for his seemingly effortless perfection, even keeping a list of "Q's Flaws" with an arbitrary fourth entry just to humanize him. By accidentally witnessing Q's painful, cowardly failure to deliver bad news to a colleague, the narrator finally gets a real "fourth entry"—seeing that Q's greatest strength (his desire to be kind and gentle) is also his fatal flaw. 

Instead of feeling triumphant, the narrator experiences a shift toward empathy and closure, realizing Q is just as "solid" and flawed as anyone else. By choosing to remain anonymous in the pool and swimming toward the "deep end," the narrator both protects Q's dignity and symbolically moves past his own decade-long stagnation and envy. All thematic and emotional threads are tied up purposefully.
